30 Why can an observable interference pattern never be obtained between two monochromatic
beams of light from different lamps?
A
The frequency of the light from the two lamps can never be the same.
B
The light from the two lamps can never be coherent.
C
The temperature of the filaments of the two lamps used can never be the same.
D
The wavelength of the light from the two lamps must always be different.

hints: Notice the key wording: two monochromatic beams from different lamps - focus on whether their waves can keep a fixed relationship at a point.
Recall that observable two-source interference needs coherent sources with the same frequency and a constant phase difference $\Delta \phi$.
Think about how light is emitted by billions of independent atoms in each lamp and whether the phase difference between the two lamps could stay constant in time.
walkthrough: Identify the setup: two separate monochromatic light sources illuminating the same region, asking why no stable interference fringes are ever seen.
State the condition for observable interference: the two waves must be coherent, meaning same frequency $f$ and wavelength $\lambda$ with constant phase difference over time.
Explain emission from a lamp: each atom emits short wave trains at random times, so the phase of each lamp jumps randomly billions of times per second.

Show the consequence: the phase difference between lamp 1 and lamp 2 changes randomly and rapidly, so positions of constructive and destructive superposition shift faster than the eye can follow and average out to uniform illumination.
Check the distractors: same $f$ and $\lambda$ can be selected with filters, and filament temperature does not control phase constancy, so A, C and D do not explain the failure.
Therefore the fundamental reason is lack of coherence. This is option B

A.explanation: Two separate lamps could in principle emit the same frequency if filtered to be monochromatic, so frequency mismatch is not the fundamental barrier.

B.explanation: Independent lamps emit light with randomly changing phase differences, so they are not coherent and cannot give a stable observable pattern.

C.explanation: Filament temperature affects intensity and spectrum, but stable interference depends on phase relationship, not on equal temperatures.

D.explanation: Both beams are stated to be monochromatic and could have the same wavelength $\lambda$, so wavelength difference is not the necessary reason.
